_comment: APEX TXT VERIFICATION TOKENS (wp_recon.classify_txt_verifications). A site/mail verification value in a domain's TXT record (e.g. '<provider>-verification=<uuid>') is issued per customer account, so two domains carrying the same token are owner-link candidates (rung class txt.verification). Some providers instead publish ONE constant value for every customer — emitting that would cluster every tenant. So a token becomes an owner edge only after the provider's OWN zone was resolved and the token is absent there; a token present in the provider zone is a provider-wide constant and is never emitted; a token whose provider zone is unknown or unresolvable is ingested as a lead fact, not an edge. Add a provider to provider_zones when you see its verification record format.

token_shapes._comment: Case-insensitive regexes for the token VALUE inside a TXT record: UUID-shaped and long hex (32+ chars). Anything else (base64 site-verification strings, SPF mechanisms) is out of scope here — page-level verification meta tags are handled by wp_extract.VERIFICATION_META.

provider_zones._comment: Provider DENYLIST + zone map: provider keyword (matched as a whole segment of the TXT record's label before '=', or via an MX host under the zone) -> the provider's own zone whose TXT records are checked. A token that also appears in this zone is a provider-wide constant, never an owner link.

ignored_prefixes._comment: TXT record prefixes that are mail-policy records, never verification tokens (lowercase, matched at the start of the record).
